subject: Science
title: Keep a rock test fair
objective_verbatim: Plan and carry out a simple fair test on rocks.
reading_age_est: rough ARI grade 2.03 on 652 pupil-visible words; heuristic age guide 8.03 years, not a formal reading-age test
pupil_words: I am learning to keep a rock test the same each time.
success_criteria: I can name what we change.
I can name what stays the same.
I can record what I see.

vocab.definition: a check with one planned change
vocab.example: I use three drops each time.

retrieval.question: Name one raw and one made item.
Why can slate suit a roof?
retrieval.answer: A suitable slate can form thin roof pieces.

retrieval.question: How can food help a body?

stages.pupil_text: See two rocks and a dropper.
stages.adult_text: Offer a safe kit choice and short first–then cue.

stages.pupil_text: Think back. Say, sign or point.
stages.adult_text: Ask three low-stakes prior questions; answers in note.
Pre-teach words; show the full model; ask the show-me check.

stages.pupil_text: Plan and run the same steps.
stages.adult_text: Hand over the missing step; offer F or H route. Reset once.

stages.pupil_text: All of us show one choice.
stages.adult_text: Take all pupil responses at once; use decision rule and parallel hinge.

stages.pupil_text: Test two rocks. Record what you see.
stages.adult_text: Choose one adult for supported pupils, one for group; swap across the week.

stages.pupil_text: Check two rows. Hear a next step.
stages.adult_text: Give VF and one NS(+); invite one self-edit. Reset once.
Hear feedback and next step, choose next start, then one-minute reset.

worked_example.full: A gets three drops. I wait one count. B gets the same.
worked_example.faded: A gets three drops. B gets ____ drops. I wait the same time.
worked_example.removed_step: Fill three as the water amount for rock B.
worked_example.fade_next: Remove the amount and the time prompt; pupil plans both controls.

cfu.question: Do three drops on A and ten on B keep the water amount the same?
cfu.answer: No. Use the same amount for both.

hinge.question: New samples C and D get four and nine drops. Is the water amount controlled?

options.diagnosis: Keeps the water amount equal across samples.
Removes the changed sample from the comparison.
Adds an unsupported reason for unequal amounts.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more right → move on; otherwise re-model A gets three drops. I wait one count. B gets the same. Ask the parallel hinge. No scores or answers saved.
hinge.parallel_hinge: New rocks E and F each get four drops, but E waits ten counts and F waits two. Is the wait fair? No; keep the wait the same.

misconceptions.misconception: Any water on both samples makes the test fair.
misconceptions.correction: Use the same amount for both while the sample changes.

misconceptions.misconception: The two tests must use the same rock to be fair.
misconceptions.correction: Change the rock you compare; keep water amount and time the same.

we_do.support: Place three dot counters by each rock.
we_do.stretch: Why could different sample sizes spoil this check?

tiers.F: Point to what stays the same.
tiers.H: One rock is much larger. How could you compare?

stems.M: I change ____ and keep ____ the same.
stems.H: The check may fail if ____; I will ____.

tiers.go_deeper: Drops run off an edge. Did water pass through? Fix it.
tiers.early_finisher: Find two unfair steps. Fix them.

adaptations.cognition_learning: Give a three-step visual card for keep a rock test fair; remove its last cue after a correct try.
adaptations.communication_interaction: Point to the real kit before a short spoken, signed or AAC response; wait for a turn.
adaptations.semh: Offer a private first–then cue and planned pause before the hinge; re-enter with one step.
adaptations.sensory_physical: Use a stable tray, large cards or an accessible input; no forced touch.
adaptations.eal: Rehearse a full M or H idea in any language before writing; keep the science challenge.

ta_focus.we_do: What step is missing? Show it with the kit.
ta_focus.independent: What can you do first on your own?

F.a: The tool used to add drops.
The drop count and wait time.

M.q: Are three drops and ten drops fair?
M.a: No. Give each rock the same drop count.

H.q: One sample is much larger. What will you do?
H.a: Use samples of similar size or state that size also changed.
A drop in the tray may have run off the side, not through the rock.

items.clue: Use the same tray each time

items: Three on A, ten on B

diagrams.alt: Two rock samples A and B on separate trays receive the same three drops; pictures show top, through and edge routes to inspect, not actual results.
diagrams.caption: Fair check: same drops and wait; inspect top, through and edge routes. No result is assumed. Simplified; not to scale.

practical.prediction: Will the drops act the same?
method: Add three drops to A. Wait one count.
practical.risk: Check against the school risk assessment and CLEAPSS guidance. Use clean blunt samples; control the water and dry any spill.
practical.pupil_risk: Rock edges may scratch skin; water may spill.
practical.pupil_safety: Use blunt rocks in a tray. Wipe spills. Do not taste; wash hands after.

facts.claim: A fair comparison changes the rock and keeps the water amount and waiting time consistent.
Two rocks can have different water movement, but a classroom test must report only observed results.
A drop running off an edge is not proof it passed through the rock.
Vocabulary term fair test means a check with one planned change; example: I use three drops each time.
Vocabulary term same means not changed in each try; example: I use the same water.
Vocabulary term change means make one thing different; example: I change the rock.
Vocabulary term result means what the check showed; example: A drop stayed on top.
Retrieval question from SoW C43: Name one raw and one made item. Answer: Raw rock and finished brick.
Retrieval question from SoW C42: Why can slate suit a roof? Answer: A suitable slate can form thin roof pieces.
Retrieval question from SoW C37: How can food help a body? Answer: It gives nutrition.
The “3 drops”, “Rock A” and “Rock B” labels show the same amount of water over two different samples; no result is assumed.
The “Edge” label marks one possible route; routes to inspect also include on top and through connected spaces.
Pupil-facing practical risk statement: Rock edges may scratch skin; water may spill.

stages: Arrival (5 min): See two rocks and a dropper. Staff: Offer a safe kit choice and short first–then cue.
Starter (3 min): Think back. Say, sign or point. Staff: Ask three low-stakes prior questions; answers in note.
I Do (5 min): Watch a fair water check. Staff: Pre-teach words; show the full model; ask the show-me check.
We Do (7 min): Plan and run the same steps. Staff: Hand over the missing step; offer F or H route. Reset once.
We Do 2 (5 min): All of us show one choice. Staff: Take all pupil responses at once; use decision rule and parallel hinge.
Independent (8 min): Test two rocks. Record what you see. Staff: Choose one adult for supported pupils, one for group; swap across the week.
Review (4 min): Check two rows. Hear a next step. Staff: Give VF and one NS(+); invite one self-edit. Reset once.
Exit (3 min): Say what stayed the same. Staff: Hear feedback and next step, choose next start, then one-minute reset.
